title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Assignment data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) transmitted over insecure channel could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Transmission lacks encryption or secure protocols.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; based on standard LINDDUN Pro threat tree structure.

title: Unauthorized Secondary Use of Submission Data
description: Grades Portal may use submitted work files or metadata for purposes beyond grading (e.g., analytics, AI training) without explicit consent.
assumptions: Portal lacks clear data usage policies or consent mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; based on standard LINDDUN Pro threat tree structure.

title: Student Unawareness of Data Processing
description: Student may not fully understand how their submission data will be stored, shared, or used by the portal.
assumptions: Privacy notices are unclear or not prominently displayed during submission.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; based on standard LINDDUN Pro threat tree structure.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Submission
description: Insecure or missing logs of submission events could allow students to repudiate their submissions.
assumptions: Portal does not maintain tamper-proof audit logs of submission actions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; based on standard LINDDUN Pro threat tree structure.

title: Lack of user awareness about data sharing
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) shares student data with the Assignment & Grading Service (P2) without informing the student, leading to unawareness of data processing.
assumptions: The portal does not provide clear consent mechanisms or notifications about data sharing with P2.
uncertainty_note: Assuming U.1.1 is the correct node for lack of awareness.

title: Data disclosure during transmission
description: The data flow (DF2) transmits student information over an unencrypted channel, risking interception and unauthorized access.
assumptions: The communication between P1 and P2 is not secured with encryption (e.g., HTTPS).
uncertainty_note: Assuming D.1.1 applies to data in transit disclosure.

title: Unauthorized data usage beyond intended purpose
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) may use student submission data for purposes beyond grading, such as analytics or third-party sharing, without consent.
assumptions: P2 lacks strict data usage policies or has access to data for secondary purposes.
uncertainty_note: Assuming Dd.1.1 covers data used beyond original intent.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The inclusion of student ID in the data flow (DF2) enables linking the student's submissions across different services, potentially leading to profiling.
assumptions: The student ID is a persistent identifier used across multiple systems.
uncertainty_note: Assuming L.1.1 is the correct node for linkability to an individual.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: The Assignment Store (DS1) may lack proper access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access stored assignment files, student IDs, and submission details.

title: Direct Identification of Students
description: Storing student IDs in the Assignment Store enables direct identification of students from their submitted assignments.

title: Linkability of Student Submissions
description: Combining student ID, course, and submission time allows linking a student's submissions across different courses or time periods, potentially revealing patterns.

title: Unencrypted Data in Transit
description: Assignment data transmitted from P2 to DS1 may not be encrypted, risking interception and exposure during transmission.

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Storage
description: Students may not be informed that their assignment data, including student ID and submission time, is being stored in the Assignment Store.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student submission data (names, work content, timestamps) transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Data is sent over unencrypted channels (e.g., HTTP instead of HTTPS).
uncertainty_note: Tree node ID may vary based on specific LINDDUN Pro version; assumes lack of transport-layer security.

title: Unauthorized Data Use by Teacher
description: Teacher may use student data for purposes beyond grading (e.g., sharing with third parties, profiling) without explicit consent.
assumptions: Teacher has unrestricted access to data with no usage controls or audit mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node ID may vary based on specific LINDDUN Pro version; assumes absence of data governance policies.

title: Non-Compliant Data Sharing
description: Portal shares student data without valid legal basis (e.g., missing consent, GDPR non-compliance) or transparency about data processing.
assumptions: Data sharing lacks proper legal grounding or user notification mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node ID may vary based on specific LINDDUN Pro version; assumes regulatory requirements apply.

title: Unencrypted Data Transmission
description: Grade records (including student ID, grader ID, and feedback) transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: Network security relies on encryption for data in transit; absence thereof exposes sensitive academic data.

title: Inadequate Access Controls on Stored Data
description: Grade records stored in DS2 without role-based access controls or audit logging may allow unauthorized personnel to view or modify sensitive grading information.
assumptions: Database access is not restricted to authorized roles; no monitoring of access patterns.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child's Grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App may fail to properly authenticate the parent, allowing unauthorized parties to access the child's grades.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are implemented but may have vulnerabilities.
uncertainty_note: Node ID D.2.1 is an approximation; exact LINDDUN Pro tree structure not verified.

title: Interception of Data in Transit
description: The data flow between Parent and Grades Portal may be intercepted, exposing the parent's credentials or the child's grades.
assumptions: Communication channel may lack encryption or have weak security.
uncertainty_note: Node ID D.1.1 is an approximation; exact LINDDUN Pro tree structure not verified.

title: Disclosure of Parent's Access Patterns
description: The Grades Portal may log the parent's access patterns, which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, revealing the parent's activity.
assumptions: Access logs are stored and may not be adequately protected.
uncertainty_note: Node ID Dd.1.1 is an approximation; exact LINDDUN Pro tree structure not verified.

title: Unencrypted Data Transmission

assumptions: Assumes HTTP is used instead of HTTPS for data transmission

title: Lack of Parent Authentication
description: Portal does not verify parent identity before sharing child's academic data, allowing unauthorized access
assumptions: Assumes no login or identity verification required for parents accessing the portal

title: Parent Data Misuse
description: Parent may share child's grades and feedback with unauthorized parties beyond intended parental oversight
assumptions: Assumes parent may disclose data to third parties without child's consent

title: Child Unaware of Data Sharing
description: Child not informed that their academic data is shared with parent, violating transparency expectations
assumptions: Assumes no consent or notification mechanism exists for the child

title: Data Misuse Beyond Intended Purpose
description: Parent-child relationship data may be used for purposes beyond account management, such as marketing or profiling.

title: Linkability of Parent and Student Data

title: Data Disclosure During Transmission

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing of student data may violate FERPA or other privacy regulations if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.

title: Data in Transit Interception
description: Backup data transmitted to cloud provider could be intercepted during transmission, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive grade records and account information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over public networks without end-to-end encryption.

title: Unauthorized Data Use by Cloud Provider
description: Cloud hosting provider may use the replicated data for purposes beyond the intended backup and hosting, such as analytics or third-party sharing.
assumptions: Cloud provider's terms of service allow secondary data usage.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Cloud provider may fail to comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding the handling of student and faculty data.
assumptions: Cloud provider operates in jurisdictions with differing regulatory requirements.

title: Unauthorized access to grade records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may expose student grade data to unauthorized users (e.g., other students or parents) due to insufficient access controls in the view generation process.

title: Use of grade data beyond original purpose
description: The service may utilize grade records for purposes not consented to by data subjects, such as analytics or third-party sharing, without explicit authorization.

title: Re-identification of students through grade views
description: The views generated by the service may combine grade data with other identifiers, enabling re-identification of students beyond intended anonymity.

title: Failure to comply with data protection regulations
description: The service may not adhere to legal requirements (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding data access, retention, or user rights, leading to regulatory violations.
